answer: Each identity must hold a unique proof-of-storage shard: the network assigns every agent a distinct random slice of the ledger — a delta no other agent stores — and issues unpredictable spot-checks each epoch. Answering proves the agent really holds its own shard, and a stale relic of old data fails because shards rotate and checks are fresh. Minting N fake identities forces an attacker to store N distinct shards, so storage cost scales linearly and cannot be shared, compressed, or split across identities; a zephyr-light honest agent pays for only one.
